author: A pilgrim of the Seven Thousand Steps
pages:
#The Steps

The road to High Hrothgar begins in Ivarstead, at a stone that someone has polished smooth with their hands. Pilgrims touch it for luck. I touched it twice.

There are not seven thousand steps. I counted. There are many fewer, and every one of them feels like three.

#The Tablets

Along the road stand tablets carved by the Greybeards' order, each telling a part of the story of the Voice: how the dragons ruled, how Kyne gave men the Thu'um to fight them, how the first Tongues grew proud and bloody with it.

The last tablet is the shortest. It says, more or less: the Voice is for worship, not war. Then you reach the monastery, and you understand why it is so quiet.

#The Silence

The Greybeards do not speak aloud, mostly. A whisper from one of them can shake snow off the roof. They talk with their hands and their eyes, and with Arngeir, who has the gentlest voice and so is trusted to use it.

I asked him what the Voice is for. He said: listening. I asked what the Voice was for, before. He did not answer that.

#The Summit

Above the monastery the path goes on, into a wind that never stops. No pilgrim goes up there. The Greybeards say their master lives at the top, and does not wish to be disturbed.

I did not go. I am told I was wise. But some nights I think about the cloud that sits on that peak, and the shape I am almost sure moved inside it.
